canonical_name: Kennedy-Lugar Youth Exchange and Study (YES) Program — Türkiye
organizer: U.S. Department of State, Bureau of Educational and Cultural Affairs; managed in Türkiye by AFS-USA in partnership with the U.S. Embassy Public Affairs Office
organizer_domain_provenance: PARTIALLY ESTABLISHED. yesprograms.org is the programme's own site and self-identifies as the Kennedy-Lugar YES programme sponsored by the U.S. Department of State. Government corroboration exists at https://exchanges.state.gov/non-us/program/kennedy-lugar-youth-exchange-study-yes (a .gov domain), which was surfaced via search but timed out when fetched and is therefore recorded as an unfetched lead rather than as evidence. The .gov page should be read to complete provenance before ingestion.
prerequisites: Turkish citizenship, and NOT holding U.S. citizenship or U.S. permanent residency. Minimum GPA of 70. Applicants cover the cost of their passport, medical examinations and personal spending.
program_dates: An academic year in the United States
duration: 10 to 11 months living with a host family and attending a U.S. high school
cost: No programme fee — the scholarship is fully funded. Students pay only for passport, medical examinations and personal spending money.
financial_aid: Fully funded scholarship covering round-trip airfare from the home country to the United States, health insurance, a monthly stipend, host family placement and pre-departure orientation costs.
selection_process: Competitive selection administered locally; the Istanbul office is reachable on +90 212 232 05 04. The official page does not publish selection stages or an acceptance rate.
award_or_output: A fully funded academic year in the United States, living with a host family and attending an American high school
research_notes: STALE-CYCLE CATCH — the single most important note on this record. The official Türkiye page states applicants must be 'between the ages of 15-17 years (born between 15 August 2008 and 15 August 2010)' and enrolled in grades 9-11 'during the 2024-25 academic year'. Those birth-date windows belong to the 2024-2025 recruitment cycle and are ALREADY TWO CYCLES STALE at the 2026-08-21 retrieval date. I have deliberately NOT carried the 2008-2010 birth years into the age_range field, and have NOT recalculated them forward to 2026 — recalculating would be fabrication. age_range records only the durable '15-17' band with an explicit caveat. Anyone ingesting this must re-read the page for the live cycle's birth-date window. VERIFIED and durable across cycles: the Turkish-citizenship requirement, the exclusion of U.S. citizens and permanent residents, the GPA 70 minimum, the 10-11 month duration, the full funding breakdown, and AFS-USA as the in-country manager. UNKNOWN, not guessed: application open and close dates for any cycle — the official page explicitly declines to publish them and directs applicants to the Istanbul office. CATEGORY CHOICE: filed as fellowship for consistency with ORYN's existing Congress-Bundestag Youth Exchange (CBYX) record, which is a directly analogous State-Department-funded secondary-school exchange already categorised as fellowship. Fellowship is ORYN's single thinnest category (2 live rows) and Türkiye is the top-priority geography, so this record is high-value despite the stale cycle.

canonical_name: Erasmus+ Mobility for VET Learners and School Pupils
aliases: Erasmus+ traineeships abroad for vocational learners
organizer: European Commission (Erasmus+ programme), delivered through National Agencies and participating schools/VET providers
organizer_domain_provenance: FULLY ESTABLISHED WITHOUT THIRD PARTY. Both youth.europa.eu (European Youth Portal) and erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu are official European Union domains under europa.eu, operated by the European Commission. No external provenance is required.
grade_range: School pupils (any age) and VET learners/apprentices, including upper-secondary vocational students
prerequisites: The student's school or VET institution must already participate in Erasmus+. Students CANNOT apply directly — the sending organisation applies for the grant and selects the participants. Underage participants should be accompanied by adults where necessary.
duration: Individual study or traineeship: 10 days to 1 year. Group mobility: 2 to 30 days. For participants with fewer opportunities, activities may run for a minimum of 2 days.
cost: No cost to the student — financial support is provided to the school to cover travel and participation costs
financial_aid: Erasmus+ provides financial support to schools covering travel and participation costs, explicitly so that opportunities are accessible regardless of economic background. Extra support is available for participants with special needs and for those with fewer opportunities.
selection_process: The sending school or VET provider selects participants. There is no central individual application.
award_or_output: A traineeship or apprenticeship period abroad hosted in a company, workplace (including NGOs and public organisations) or vocational school
source_title: Pupils, VET learners, teachers: go abroad with Erasmus+! – European Youth Portal
research_notes: WHY THIS RECORD MATTERS MOST: internship is ORYN's thinnest priority category (8 live rows) and secondary-school-eligible internships barely exist outside the US/UK. This is the single largest structural route by which a 16-18 year old in continental Europe — including Türkiye, which participates in Erasmus+ as a programme country — can do a genuine workplace traineeship abroad at no personal cost. VERIFIED from the official EU page: the duration bands (10 days to 1 year individual; 2-30 days group; 2-day minimum for those with fewer opportunities), the school-mediated application route, the no-direct-application rule, the funding-to-schools model, and the accompanying-adult provision for minors. DELIBERATELY LEFT NULL: country list, age range in years, and dates. Erasmus+ country eligibility and National Agency deadlines vary by country and by call year; asserting a single list or deadline here would be false precision. The 2026 Programme Guide (https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/sites/default/files/2025-11/programme-guide-2026_en.pdf) is the authoritative source for the current call and was NOT fetched in this session. STRUCTURAL NOTE, same as the JA record: this is an umbrella mechanism, not a bookable opportunity. The correct counselling action is 'ask your school whether it holds an Erasmus+ accreditation', not 'apply here'. Modelling it as a directly-applicable opportunity would mislead students.

organizer: The Toronto-Dominion Bank (TD), administered with Universities Canada and the CT Foundation
organizer_domain_provenance: ESTABLISHED. The terms and conditions PDF is hosted on td.com, the Toronto-Dominion Bank's own corporate domain, and the document names 'The Toronto-Dominion Bank (TD)' as programme owner. The document independently names Universities Canada as co-administrator and cites the Universities Canada privacy policy at univcan.ca — Universities Canada being the national association of Canadian universities. Two mutually-corroborating institutional identifiers appear inside the primary document itself.
grade_range: Final year of high school (outside Quebec) or final year of CEGEP (in Quebec)
prerequisites: Minimum overall grade average of 75% outside Quebec, or a minimum R score of 26 in Quebec, in the most recently completed school year. Must be a Canadian citizen, permanent resident, or hold protected person status under the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (protected persons must also hold a study permit). Must be available for an interview on a day chosen by TD. Employees of TD and its subsidiaries and their children are explicitly ineligible.
financial_aid: The award is itself the aid. Maximum value CAD 70,000 over four years, broken down as: tuition paid directly to the approved school, up to CAD 10,000 per year for four years; living expenses paid directly to the recipient at CAD 7,500 per year for four years; and an offer of summer employment with TD for four summers, subject to the recipient being legally entitled to work in Canada. The award cannot be held alongside other financial awards totalling more than CAD 50,000 over four years, nor with any scholarship from another Canadian financial institution.
selection_process: Written application with essays on community leadership, three letters of recommendation, and a finalist interview. Judged by a selection committee alongside TD, CT Foundation and Universities Canada. NOTE: the essay count and reference count come from secondary sources, not from the terms PDF; the PDF verifies only that an interview is required.
required_materials: Program application form plus accompanying documents; availability for interview
award_or_output: Up to CAD 70,000 over four years toward Canadian post-secondary education, plus four summers of TD employment
source_title: TD Scholarships for Community Leadership — 2025/2026 Terms and Conditions
research_notes: FILENAME-VERSUS-CONTENT TRAP, FLAGGED: the PDF's URL ends in '...-2026-eng.pdf' but the document's own title block reads '2025/2026 Terms and Conditions' and every substantive clause refers to 'The 2025/2026 Scholarship'. The document content governs, so latest_verified_cycle is 2025/2026 and the state is VERIFIED_HISTORICAL. Trusting the filename would have mislabelled this as a current 2026 cycle. No 2026/2027 terms document was located. METHOD NOTE: this PDF returned as binary through the fetch tool and was unreadable as text; the clauses cited here were extracted by decompressing the PDF's own content streams locally, so every quoted figure comes from the primary document rather than from any summary of it. VERIFIED verbatim from the terms: the five eligibility clauses (3a-3e), the CAD 70,000 cap, the CAD 10,000/year tuition and CAD 7,500/year living-expense components, the four-summer TD employment offer, and the CAD 50,000 concurrent-award restriction. UNKNOWN, not guessed: application open/close dates and the number of scholarships awarded — neither appears in the terms document, and the widely-circulated 'September 3 to October 22' window comes from secondary sources tied to an earlier year, so it is not recorded. TIMING RELEVANCE: if TD repeats its usual autumn pattern the next window would fall shortly after this retrieval date, which makes re-checking the live TD page time-sensitive — but that pattern is an observation, not a verified date.

canonical_name: The Duke of Edinburgh's International Award — Türkiye
aliases: The International Award for Young People-Türkiye
organizer: TİKAV — Türkiye İnsan Kaynakları Eğitim ve Sağlık Vakfı (Turkey Human Resources Education and Health Foundation), as National Authority under licence from the International Award Foundation
organizer_domain_provenance: ESTABLISHED VIA PARENT ORGANISATION. The International Award Foundation, the global licensor, maintains a Türkiye location page at https://intaward.org/location/turkey/ and has published coverage of a Duke of Edinburgh visit to Türkiye on intaward.org. The Turkish operator's own site intaward.org.tr states that TİKAV 'became the sole National Authority of The Duke of Edinburgh's International Award in Türkiye' as of June 2013 under a licence agreement signed with the International Award Foundation in England. The .org.tr domain mirrors the licensor's own intaward.org domain, and ORYN already holds two sibling national-operator records (Australia, Hong Kong) confirming this national-licensee structure. NOTE: the intaward.org Türkiye location page was surfaced via search and NOT fetched in this session.
prerequisites: Participation is normally arranged through a licensed centre such as a school. The official page does not state entry prerequisites beyond the age band.
duration: Varies by Award level (Bronze, Silver, Gold); the official page does not state the minimum durations per level
selection_process: Non-competitive — the Award is a participation framework, not a selective programme.
award_or_output: Bronze, Silver or Gold Award certification recognising achievement across volunteering, physical recreation, skills and an expedition
source_title: The History of The Award – The International Award for Young People-Türkiye
research_notes: VERIFIED from the Turkish national operator's official page: TİKAV as sole National Authority since June 2013, the licence relationship with the International Award Foundation in England, the 14-25 age band, and the existence of Bronze/Silver/Gold levels. UNKNOWN and left null rather than filled from general knowledge: the participation fee, the minimum duration for each Award level, and the list of licensed centres in Türkiye. I specifically did NOT import the Bronze/Silver/Gold section durations that the Award publishes globally, because the Türkiye page does not state them and national operators can vary — that would have been prior knowledge dressed as sourced fact. VALUE: volunteering is ORYN's single thinnest category with 1 live row, and Türkiye is the top-priority geography, so this record closes the sharpest gap in the table. It also completes a coherent sibling set — ORYN already holds the Australia and Hong Kong national Awards, so a counsellor can now recognise the Award framework across three markets. verification_state is VERIFIED_CURRENT because the Award is an evergreen open-enrolment framework with no application cycle to go stale; there is no cycle date to verify against.
